component.name: Gifkino
component.summary: Edit animated GIFs along the time axis

description.p: Gifkino is a GIF editor for Linux. Open an animated GIF, an image, or a video, add overlays to frames, then export an optimized GIF.

ul.li: Opens GIFs, still images and videos, with a large clip offered at a smaller recommended size before it is decoded.

Overlays scoped to frame ranges: text, shapes (rectangle, ellipse, arrow) and images, placed on the frames you pick. Drag to move them on the canvas, hold Alt to rotate, Shift to keep the aspect ratio, Ctrl to resize from the center.
Frame list editing: reorder, duplicate, delete, retime, cut, copy and paste, drop one frame in every N, and smart-drop the frames that move the least.
Crop, resize, rotate and flip, applied across the whole animation.
A timeline that zooms, with overlay bands showing what covers what.
Undo and redo over every edit, including scoped overlay changes.
Translated interface: English, German and Japanese.
Optimized GIF export.

description.p: Frame delays stay where they were set.

ul.li: Smart remove spreads its removals out instead of turning a slow pan into one long hold and a jump
A delay typed into the sidebar is applied to the frame it was typed for, even when another frame is clicked before pressing Enter

description.p: The menu's About item opens a dialog.

ul.li: About has three sections: Details with the version and the repository, Feedback, and Licenses
Feedback leads with the issue tracker and offers a one-minute form for anyone without a GitHub account
Licenses names Gifkino's MIT code, the GTK and libadwaita stack, and the bundled ffmpeg and gifsicle programs

description.p: Exports report progress, and overlays copy across frames.

ul.li: Exporting shows the same frame-count progress bar as importing and resizing, instead of silence until the done toast
An overlay's context menu copies it onto the selected frames, or all frames when the selection is narrow
The colour button opens a popover picker sized to its content instead of the stock dialog

description.p: Video import asks how the clip should land, whatever its size.

ul.li: Every video goes through the import dialog, not only one that has to be shrunk
New advanced options: trim by timecode or frame number, drop one frame in every N, and lift the memory limit for a single import
The custom import size carries an aspect-ratio lock, as the resize dialog does
Memory is the only import ceiling; a hidden 2000-frame cap that refused long clips is gone
Screen recording is out of scope, and the disabled Record button is gone with it
